The shrine's summer festival stands out in Kanazawa for its magnitude and splendor, and has been labeled an intangible folk cultural asset of Kanazawa City. [[Maeda Toshiie]] promoted Noh, and his son revived its practice at this shrine.https://www.city.kanazawa.ishikawa.jp/f-living/english/KanazawaTradCulture_EN.pdf ==Japanese content== [[File:Noh stage Ohnominato jinja2.jpg|thumb|200px|A Noh stage where {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} is performed]] '''Ōnominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Kanazawa City|ja|金沢市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|qq=draft}}, enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. == History == In {{ill|Shinki era|ja|神亀|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|Year 727|ja|727th year|qq=draft}}), a man from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|qq=draft}} named Sana (さな) discovered {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} during a voyage. He established a small shrine next to an existing {{ill|Shinmei Shrine|ja|神明社|qq=draft}} (dedicated to {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft}}) at Ōno-shō Masagoyama Saonohayashi. From this enshrinement, the shrine became known as Ōnominato Shrine, serving as the guardian deity of the harbor of Ōno-gō (the old {{ill|Miyakoshi|ja|宮腰|qq=draft}} area, now {{ill|Kanaiwa-chō|ja|金石町|lt_ja=金石町|lt=Kanaiwa-chō|qq=draft}}). In {{ill|Tenpyō|ja|天平|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|729|ja|729th year|qq=draft}}), it was granted the title "Sanatake Daimyōjin" (佐那武大明神). During {{ill|Enchō (Japan)|ja|延長|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft}}), the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft}} listed it as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Kaga District (Kaga Province)|ja|加賀郡 (加賀国)|lt_ja=加賀郡|lt=Kaga District|qq=draft}}, one of the 2133 recognized {{ill|Imperial shrines of national significance (Kunpeisha)|ja|国幣小社|qq=draft}}. Historically, it was also known as Sanatake Ōmiya Daimyōjin or {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft}} Myōjin. By the late {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft}}, the name "Ōnominato Shrine" had faded, replaced by "Sanatake-sha." Around that time, the shrine became a prominent subordinate shrine of the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (noted in the text {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft}}). Today, the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine on the precincts is a remnant of this history. In {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|1252|ja|1252nd year|qq=draft}}), a fire forced the shrine to be relocated from Furū-Ōno to the Rikyū Hachiman Shrine area in Teranaka-machi (its current location), approximately eight chō (roughly 872 meters) east. During the {{ill|Sengoku Period|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} it fell into ruin but was later restored by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家|qq=draft}}. From {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|qq=draft}} 9 ({{ill|1604|ja|1604th year|qq=draft}}), the performance of {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} became an annual tradition initiated by {{ill|Maeda Toshinaga|ja|前田利長|qq=draft}}. The shrine buildings were constructed by {{ill|Maeda Toshitsune|ja|前田利常|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|qq=draft}} 16 ({{ill|1639|ja|1639th year|qq=draft}}). In {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft}} 18 ({{ill|1885|ja|1885th year|qq=draft}}), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft}}, and in {{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft}} 41 ({{ill|1966|ja|1966th year|qq=draft}}), it was recognized as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft}}. In Shōwa 57 ({{ill|1982|ja|1982nd year|qq=draft}}), it was designated as a cultural property by Ishikawa Prefecture. Every year, the grand festival held from August 1 to 3 reenacts the shrine’s earlier era when it stood in Ōno-gō for 525 years. A portable shrine (mikoshi) is moved to a temporary hall on the seashore, an event widely known as the summer festival of {{ill|Kanaiwa (Kanazawa City)|ja|金石 (金沢市)|lt_ja=金石|lt=Kanaiwa|qq=draft}}. == Origin of the name and Related Aspects == It is said that the name "Sana" (佐那), the man who first enshrined Sarutahiko Ōkami, is the origin of the shrine’s historical appellations. According to a folkloric interpretation, Sana may refer to "sanagi" (a type of bell, as mentioned in the {{ill|Ruijū Myōgishō|ja|類聚名義抄|qq=draft}}), implying a connection to ironworking technology passed on from northern Japan by gold merchants from Ōshū. Additionally, some theories connect Sana to the deity {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}} worshipped at this shrine, linking it to Hakusan faith. Another theory states that Sana is derived from {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft}}, a sand dune once located along the southern bank of the {{ill|Saigawa River (Ishikawa)|ja|犀川 (石川県)|lt_ja=犀川|lt=Saigawa River|qq=draft}}, near what is now Kanaiwa-chō in Kanazawa City. Originally located at the foot of Saradake by the port of Ōno, Ōnominato Shrine is said to have been lost to the sea due to repeated storms and tidal erosion. By the early modern period, even the name "Saradake" had vanished. According to the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft}}, Taira no Moritoshi (越中前司{{ill|Taira no Moritoshi|ja|平盛俊|qq=draft}}) once encamped at Saradake in Miyakoshi (Miyano-koshi). In the {{ill|Dai Nihonshi|ja|大日本史|qq=draft}} (Vol. 230, Biographies 157, concerning Minamoto no Yoshinaka), citing the {{ill|Gempei Seisuiki|ja|源平盛衰記|qq=draft}} and Heike Monogatari, there is a passage: ''"Yorimori barely escaped, regrouped scattered troops in Kaga, and held Miyakoshi Saradake. Minamoto no Yukie took his forces toward Mount Shio, suffering unfavorable battle conditions. Hearing this, Yoshinaka led forty thousand cavalry there. Taira no Moritoshi, upon hearing of Yorimori's defeat, fled to Saradake. Yoshinaka then advanced north into Kaga..."'' == Connection with Hakusan Faith == Although the deity enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine does not overlap with that of the {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|qq=draft}}, there was a time when it served as a significant subordinate shrine to the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (as noted in {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft}}). This heritage is reflected in the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine within the precincts. The "{{ill|Kaga Shoshinshaengi|ja|加賀諸神社縁起|qq=draft}}" states the following regarding Sanatake Hakusan Gongen: ''"Sanatake Hakusan Gongen was one of the nine small shrines of Hakusan Hime Shrine’s sanctum and is said to have been a branch shrine of the main Hakusan sanctuary in ancient times. Back then, many shrine monks (shasō) served at Sanatake Hakusan, and there was a temple called 'Sanatake’s Kannon Hall.' The area was known as Teranaka due to the numerous temples, and the remains are now called Teranaka Village. The place where the Kannon Hall once stood is now called Kannondō Village. In ancient times, there were numerous shrine attendants and monks of Sanatake Hakusan living in this vicinity, but following the turmoil since the {{ill|Chōkyō|ja|長享|qq=draft}} era (1487–1488), the shrine personnel dispersed, and the halls and buildings were destroyed by war. The sacred treasures and Buddhist images were barely rescued..."'' Within the network of the {{ill|Hakusan Shichisha (Seven Shrines)|ja|白山七社|qq=draft}}, there are three shrines of the Middle Sanctuary: the main Middle Shrine, the Separate Shrine, and the Saranomiya (also read as Saromiya). Saranomiya (佐羅宮), located in present-day {{ill|Hakusan City|ja|白山市|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Sara|ja|佐良|qq=draft}}, is identified with the {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. The Heian-period text "Hakusan no Ki" describes Saranomiya as follows: ''"From here belongs Saranomiya. There is another treasured shrine called Sara Daimyōjin, whose honji-butsu (original Buddhist form) is Fudō Myōō. In the fifth year of Tengen (壬午), a sanctuary building was first constructed. The small shrines (Fugen, Monju) are known as Hayamatsu and Namimatsu (Yone-mochi Kongō Dōji). The Taiko no Taki has six sons. The main Buddha is Dainichi Nyorai. In Chōhō 1 (己亥), two buildings were constructed, each five-bay by two-bay, and one lecture hall was begun. Another shrine, called Rokkusho-dō, exists, with two buildings called On’ya. There is also another shrine called Sakaime Myōjin. Azusazawa is Hiraiwa."'' In another document, "Kaga Hakusan Denki no Koto," Saranomiya is described as follows: ''"The sixth is Saranomiya. Its honji-butsu is Shō Kannon (Noble Kannon), and its manifestation is the earth deity Ugayafukiaezu no Mikoto, the fifth divine ancestor."'' A legend recorded in the {{ill|Gikeiki|ja|義経記|qq=draft}} "Aibatsuyama no Koto," composed sometime between the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft}}, provides related lore: ''Benkei said, "…This place is called 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain) because, in Kaga Province, at a place known as Shimo-Shirayama (Lower Hakusan), there resided a female deity in a palace called Ryūgū no Miya. Having spent many years since she first appeared to Karasaki no Myōjin in the capital of Shiga, she became pregnant. Approaching her due month, she decided to return to her homeland to give birth. While traveling through this mountain’s peak (known as the zennjō [zenjō, summit]), she suddenly felt labor pains. The deity supporting her said, 'Your delivery is near,' and cradled her waist, and so the child was immediately born. At that time, the afterbirth blood spilled, hence the name 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain). Now you understand the origin of Arashii no Yama, Arachi no Yama." Hearing this, Lord Yoshitsune laughed and said, "Indeed, I knew this as well."'' The child born there is said to be Sara no Ōji (Prince Sara), suggesting a connection with {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. Additionally, since Sara, Sana, and Sara(dake) appear phonetically and contextually related, it hints at a potential connection between Hakusan Hime Shrine and Ōnominato Shrine. One interpretation is that Sanatake-sha, enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine, was once a subordinate shrine of the Hakusan main sanctuary. The princess deity and Karasaki Myōjin’s child, Prince Sara, may have been worshipped at Saradake as {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}}, linking these shrines and locations together. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation, the place name "Miyakoshi" can be understood as "the shrine (miya) at the foot (koshi) of a mountain," referring either to the base of Hakusan or Saradake. In ancient Japanese, "koshi" means the foot of a mountain, reinforcing this theory. == festivals == * '''Grand festival:''' Traditionally held from {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft}} to {{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft}}, it now ends on the first Sunday of August. During this time, a temporary hall is erected at the shrine’s original location, and the mikoshi is moved there, recreating the scene of its ancient enshrinement. * '''Shinji Noh''' (May 15): Alongside the grand festival, ritual Noh performances are held annually on {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}}. ==References== {{reflist}} == External Links == * [http://oonominato.web.fc2.com/ Official Website of Ōnominato Shrine] (in Japanese) {{Normdaten}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{translated page|ja|大野湊神社|version=101992149|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Onominato Shrine}} {{Draft categories| [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] }} [[every:Onominato Shrine]] [[every:Onominato Shrine|Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[sn:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:draft:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:Onominato Shrine]] [[fr:Onominato-jinja]] [[fr:User:Onominato Shrine]] [[ja:%E5%A4%A7%E9%87%8E%E6%B9%8A%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[sn:Onominato Shrine]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]]

It is related to {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|en|Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=draft}} == History == According to [[Japanese mythology]] {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en}}, the main god of the shrine, was discovered in the sea during a voyage by an individual named Sana from [[Mutsu Province]] in the year 727. Upon enshrining the deity in the gold stone Masagoyama pole forest, it was bestowed the name "Sanatake Daimeijin."enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. The shrine was originally on a beach, but the shrine was moved to its present site in 1252 following a fire that destroyed the original structure. The shrine faced destruction again during the turmoil of the [[Ikkō-ikki|Ikko-ikki rebellions]]. It was restored by [[Maeda Toshiie]] in 1586. Later, in 1639, [[Maeda Toshiie]], the third feudal lord, constructed three primary shrines within its precincts. In 1872, it became a village shrine and subsequently gained reverence in 22 neighboring towns, including Kanaiwa Town. By 1879, it received the status of a prefectural shrine. Presently, it stands as an individual shrine affiliated with the Association of Shinto Shrines. In {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|1252|ja|1252nd year|qq=draft}}), a fire forced the shrine to be relocated from Furū-Ōno to the Rikyū Hachiman Shrine area in Teranaka-machi (its current location), approximately eight chō (roughly 872 meters) east. During the {{ill|Sengoku Period|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} it fell into ruin but was later restored by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家|qq=draft}}. From {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|qq=draft}} 9 ({{ill|1604|ja|1604th year|qq=draft}}), the performance of {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} became an annual tradition initiated by {{ill|Maeda Toshinaga|ja|前田利長|qq=draft}}. The shrine buildings were constructed by {{ill|Maeda Toshitsune|ja|前田利常|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|qq=draft}} 16 ({{ill|1639|ja|1639th year|qq=draft}}). In {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft}} 18 ({{ill|1885|ja|1885th year|qq=draft}}), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft}}, and in {{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft}} 41 ({{ill|1966|ja|1966th year|qq=draft}}), it was recognized as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft}}. In Shōwa 57 ({{ill|1982|ja|1982nd year|qq=draft}}), it was designated as a cultural property by Ishikawa Prefecture. Every year, the grand festival held from August 1 to 3 reenacts the shrine’s earlier era when it stood in Ōno-gō for 525 years. A portable shrine (mikoshi) is moved to a temporary hall on the seashore, an event widely known as the summer festival of {{ill|Kanaiwa (Kanazawa City)|ja|金石 (金沢市)|lt_ja=金石|lt=Kanaiwa|qq=draft}}. == Origin of the name and Related Aspects == It is said that the name "Sana" (佐那), the man who first enshrined Sarutahiko Ōkami, is the origin of the shrine’s historical appellations. According to a folkloric interpretation, Sana may refer to "sanagi" (a type of bell, as mentioned in the {{ill|Ruijū Myōgishō|ja|類聚名義抄|qq=draft}}), implying a connection to ironworking technology passed on from northern Japan by gold merchants from Ōshū. Additionally, some theories connect Sana to the deity {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}} worshipped at this shrine, linking it to Hakusan faith. Another theory states that Sana is derived from {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft}}, a sand dune once located along the southern bank of the {{ill|Saigawa River (Ishikawa)|ja|犀川 (石川県)|lt_ja=犀川|lt=Saigawa River|qq=draft}}, near what is now Kanaiwa-chō in Kanazawa City. Originally located at the foot of Saradake by the port of Ōno, Ōnominato Shrine is said to have been lost to the sea due to repeated storms and tidal erosion. By the early modern period, even the name "Saradake" had vanished. According to the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft}}, Taira no Moritoshi (越中前司{{ill|Taira no Moritoshi|ja|平盛俊|qq=draft}}) once encamped at Saradake in Miyakoshi (Miyano-koshi). In the {{ill|Dai Nihonshi|ja|大日本史|qq=draft}} (Vol. 230, Biographies 157, concerning Minamoto no Yoshinaka), citing the {{ill|Gempei Seisuiki|ja|源平盛衰記|qq=draft}} and Heike Monogatari, there is a passage: ''"Yorimori barely escaped, regrouped scattered troops in Kaga, and held Miyakoshi Saradake. Minamoto no Yukie took his forces toward Mount Shio, suffering unfavorable battle conditions. Hearing this, Yoshinaka led forty thousand cavalry there. Taira no Moritoshi, upon hearing of Yorimori's defeat, fled to Saradake. Yoshinaka then advanced north into Kaga..."'' == Connection with Hakusan Faith == Although the deity enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine does not overlap with that of the {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|qq=draft}}, there was a time when it served as a significant subordinate shrine to the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (as noted in {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft}}). This heritage is reflected in the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine within the precincts. The "{{ill|Kaga Shoshinshaengi|ja|加賀諸神社縁起|qq=draft}}" states the following regarding Sanatake Hakusan Gongen: ''"Sanatake Hakusan Gongen was one of the nine small shrines of Hakusan Hime Shrine’s sanctum and is said to have been a branch shrine of the main Hakusan sanctuary in ancient times. Back then, many shrine monks (shasō) served at Sanatake Hakusan, and there was a temple called 'Sanatake’s Kannon Hall.' The area was known as Teranaka due to the numerous temples, and the remains are now called Teranaka Village. The place where the Kannon Hall once stood is now called Kannondō Village. In ancient times, there were numerous shrine attendants and monks of Sanatake Hakusan living in this vicinity, but following the turmoil since the {{ill|Chōkyō|ja|長享|qq=draft}} era (1487–1488), the shrine personnel dispersed, and the halls and buildings were destroyed by war. The sacred treasures and Buddhist images were barely rescued..."'' Within the network of the {{ill|Hakusan Shichisha (Seven Shrines)|ja|白山七社|qq=draft}}, there are three shrines of the Middle Sanctuary: the main Middle Shrine, the Separate Shrine, and the Saranomiya (also read as Saromiya). Saranomiya (佐羅宮), located in present-day {{ill|Hakusan City|ja|白山市|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Sara|ja|佐良|qq=draft}}, is identified with the {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. The Heian-period text "Hakusan no Ki" describes Saranomiya as follows: ''"From here belongs Saranomiya. There is another treasured shrine called Sara Daimyōjin, whose honji-butsu (original Buddhist form) is Fudō Myōō. In the fifth year of Tengen (壬午), a sanctuary building was first constructed. The small shrines (Fugen, Monju) are known as Hayamatsu and Namimatsu (Yone-mochi Kongō Dōji). The Taiko no Taki has six sons. The main Buddha is Dainichi Nyorai. In Chōhō 1 (己亥), two buildings were constructed, each five-bay by two-bay, and one lecture hall was begun. Another shrine, called Rokkusho-dō, exists, with two buildings called On’ya. There is also another shrine called Sakaime Myōjin. Azusazawa is Hiraiwa."'' In another document, "Kaga Hakusan Denki no Koto," Saranomiya is described as follows: ''"The sixth is Saranomiya. Its honji-butsu is Shō Kannon (Noble Kannon), and its manifestation is the earth deity Ugayafukiaezu no Mikoto, the fifth divine ancestor."'' A legend recorded in the {{ill|Gikeiki|ja|義経記|qq=draft}} "Aibatsuyama no Koto," composed sometime between the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft}}, provides related lore: ''Benkei said, "…This place is called 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain) because, in Kaga Province, at a place known as Shimo-Shirayama (Lower Hakusan), there resided a female deity in a palace called Ryūgū no Miya. Having spent many years since she first appeared to Karasaki no Myōjin in the capital of Shiga, she became pregnant. Approaching her due month, she decided to return to her homeland to give birth. While traveling through this mountain’s peak (known as the zennjō [zenjō, summit]), she suddenly felt labor pains. The deity supporting her said, 'Your delivery is near,' and cradled her waist, and so the child was immediately born. At that time, the afterbirth blood spilled, hence the name 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain). Now you understand the origin of Arashii no Yama, Arachi no Yama." Hearing this, Lord Yoshitsune laughed and said, "Indeed, I knew this as well."'' The child born there is said to be Sara no Ōji (Prince Sara), suggesting a connection with {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. Additionally, since Sara, Sana, and Sara(dake) appear phonetically and contextually related, it hints at a potential connection between Hakusan Hime Shrine and Ōnominato Shrine. One interpretation is that Sanatake-sha, enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine, was once a subordinate shrine of the Hakusan main sanctuary. The princess deity and Karasaki Myōjin’s child, Prince Sara, may have been worshipped at Saradake as {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}}, linking these shrines and locations together. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation, the place name "Miyakoshi" can be understood as "the shrine (miya) at the foot (koshi) of a mountain," referring either to the base of Hakusan or Saradake. In ancient Japanese, "koshi" means the foot of a mountain, reinforcing this theory. == festivals == * '''Grand festival:''' Traditionally held from {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft}} to {{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft}}, it now ends on the first Sunday of August. During this time, a temporary hall is erected at the shrine’s original location, and the mikoshi is moved there, recreating the scene of its ancient enshrinement. * '''Shinji Noh''' (May 15): Alongside the grand festival, ritual Noh performances are held annually on {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}}. ==References== {{reflist}} == External Links == * [http://oonominato.web.fc2.com/ Official Website of Ōnominato Shrine] (in Japanese) {{Normdaten}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{translated page|ja|大野湊神社|version=101992149|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{Draft categories| [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] }} [[every:Onominato Shrine]] [[every:Onominato Shrine|Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[sn:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:draft:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:Onominato Shrine]] [[fr:Onominato-jinja]] [[fr:User:Onominato Shrine]] [[ja:%E5%A4%A7%E9%87%8E%E6%B9%8A%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[sn:Onominato Shrine]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]]

{{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}}: {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}} | map = {{location map|Japan Ishikawa|label=大野湊神社|coordinates={{coord2|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E|}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E}}}} }} '''Onominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a [[Beppyo shrine]] in [[Kanazawa]], [[Ishikawa Prefecture]].{{Cite web |title=Onominato Shrine - 金沢市観光デジタルマップ {{!}} プラチナマップ |url=https://platinumaps.jp/d/kanazawa-city?s=15337&culture=en |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=プラチナマップ {{!}} platinumaps.jp - Platinumaps |language=en}} enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. It is related to {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|en|Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=draft}} == History == According to [[Japanese mythology]] {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en}}, the main god of the shrine, was discovered in the sea during a voyage by an individual named Sana from [[Mutsu Province]] in the year 727. Upon enshrining the deity in the gold stone Masagoyama pole forest, it was bestowed the name "Sanatake Daimeijin."enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. The shrine was originally on a beach, but the shrine was moved to its present site in 1252 following a fire that destroyed the original structure. The shrine faced destruction again during the turmoil of the [[Ikkō-ikki|Ikko-ikki rebellions]]. It was restored by [[Maeda Toshiie]] in 1586. Later, in 1639, [[Maeda Toshiie]], the third feudal lord, constructed three primary shrines within its precincts. In 1872, it became a village shrine and subsequently gained reverence in 22 neighboring towns, including Kanaiwa Town. By 1879, it received the status of a prefectural shrine. Presently, it stands as an individual shrine affiliated with the Association of Shinto Shrines. [[File:Ujikofuda dark reverse.jpg|thumb|An [[Ujikofuda]] from {{ill|Onominato Shrine|ja|大野湊神社|qq=draft}}]] == Subshrines == [[Hachiman shrines|Hachiman Shrine]]: Enshrines [[Hachiman]] also known as [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]]. [[Shinmei shrines|Shinmei Shrine]]: Situated to the right, this shrine is dedicated to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Okami]]. Sanabu Shrine: Positioned to the left, it venerates the Okami of Sanatake, {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en}}. == Cultural property == In 1982, the three main shrines of Onominato Shrine were declared cultural assets of Ishikawa Prefecture. The [[Chinju no Mori]] of the shrine, and its older worship hall, along with various documents, are recognized as cultural properties. The Shinto ritual Noh, emblematic of Kanazawa's traditional culture, has been staged more than 400 times since 1604. The shrine's summer festival stands out in Kanazawa for its magnitude and splendor, and has been labeled an intangible folk cultural asset of Kanazawa City. [[Maeda Toshiie]] promoted Noh, and his son revived its practice at this shrine.https://www.city.kanazawa.ishikawa.jp/f-living/english/KanazawaTradCulture_EN.pdf ==Japanese content== [[File:Noh stage Ohnominato jinja2.jpg|thumb|200px|A Noh stage where {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} is performed]] '''Ōnominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Kanazawa City|ja|金沢市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|qq=draft}}, enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. == History == In {{ill|Shinki era|ja|神亀|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|Year 727|ja|727th year|qq=draft}}), a man from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|qq=draft}} named Sana (さな) discovered {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} during a voyage. He established a small shrine next to an existing {{ill|Shinmei Shrine|ja|神明社|qq=draft}} (dedicated to {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft}}) at Ōno-shō Masagoyama Saonohayashi. Yoshinaka then advanced north into Kaga..."'' == Connection with Hakusan Faith == Although the deity enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine does not overlap with that of the {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|qq=draft}}, there was a time when it served as a significant subordinate shrine to the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (as noted in {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft}}). This heritage is reflected in the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine within the precincts. The "{{ill|Kaga Shoshinshaengi|ja|加賀諸神社縁起|qq=draft}}" states the following regarding Sanatake Hakusan Gongen: ''"Sanatake Hakusan Gongen was one of the nine small shrines of Hakusan Hime Shrine’s sanctum and is said to have been a branch shrine of the main Hakusan sanctuary in ancient times. Back then, many shrine monks (shasō) served at Sanatake Hakusan, and there was a temple called 'Sanatake’s Kannon Hall.' The area was known as Teranaka due to the numerous temples, and the remains are now called Teranaka Village. The place where the Kannon Hall once stood is now called Kannondō Village. In ancient times, there were numerous shrine attendants and monks of Sanatake Hakusan living in this vicinity, but following the turmoil since the {{ill|Chōkyō|ja|長享|qq=draft}} era (1487–1488), the shrine personnel dispersed, and the halls and buildings were destroyed by war. The sacred treasures and Buddhist images were barely rescued..."'' Within the network of the {{ill|Hakusan Shichisha (Seven Shrines)|ja|白山七社|qq=draft}}, there are three shrines of the Middle Sanctuary: the main Middle Shrine, the Separate Shrine, and the Saranomiya (also read as Saromiya). Saranomiya (佐羅宮), located in present-day {{ill|Hakusan City|ja|白山市|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Sara|ja|佐良|qq=draft}}, is identified with the {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. The Heian-period text "Hakusan no Ki" describes Saranomiya as follows: ''"From here belongs Saranomiya. There is another treasured shrine called Sara Daimyōjin, whose honji-butsu (original Buddhist form) is Fudō Myōō. In the fifth year of Tengen (壬午), a sanctuary building was first constructed. The small shrines (Fugen, Monju) are known as Hayamatsu and Namimatsu (Yone-mochi Kongō Dōji). The Taiko no Taki has six sons. The main Buddha is Dainichi Nyorai. In Chōhō 1 (己亥), two buildings were constructed, each five-bay by two-bay, and one lecture hall was begun. Another shrine, called Rokkusho-dō, exists, with two buildings called On’ya. There is also another shrine called Sakaime Myōjin. Azusazawa is Hiraiwa."'' In another document, "Kaga Hakusan Denki no Koto," Saranomiya is described as follows: ''"The sixth is Saranomiya. Its honji-butsu is Shō Kannon (Noble Kannon), and its manifestation is the earth deity Ugayafukiaezu no Mikoto, the fifth divine ancestor."'' A legend recorded in the {{ill|Gikeiki|ja|義経記|qq=draft}} "Aibatsuyama no Koto," composed sometime between the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft}}, provides related lore: ''Benkei said, "…This place is called 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain) because, in Kaga Province, at a place known as Shimo-Shirayama (Lower Hakusan), there resided a female deity in a palace called Ryūgū no Miya. Having spent many years since she first appeared to Karasaki no Myōjin in the capital of Shiga, she became pregnant. Approaching her due month, she decided to return to her homeland to give birth. While traveling through this mountain’s peak (known as the zennjō [zenjō, summit]), she suddenly felt labor pains. The deity supporting her said, 'Your delivery is near,' and cradled her waist, and so the child was immediately born. At that time, the afterbirth blood spilled, hence the name 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain). Now you understand the origin of Arashii no Yama, Arachi no Yama." Hearing this, Lord Yoshitsune laughed and said, "Indeed, I knew this as well."'' The child born there is said to be Sara no Ōji (Prince Sara), suggesting a connection with {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft}}. Additionally, since Sara, Sana, and Sara(dake) appear phonetically and contextually related, it hints at a potential connection between Hakusan Hime Shrine and Ōnominato Shrine. One interpretation is that Sanatake-sha, enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine, was once a subordinate shrine of the Hakusan main sanctuary. The princess deity and Karasaki Myōjin’s child, Prince Sara, may have been worshipped at Saradake as {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}}, linking these shrines and locations together. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation, the place name "Miyakoshi" can be understood as "the shrine (miya) at the foot (koshi) of a mountain," referring either to the base of Hakusan or Saradake. In ancient Japanese, "koshi" means the foot of a mountain, reinforcing this theory. == festivals == * '''Grand festival:''' Traditionally held from {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft}} to {{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft}}, it now ends on the first Sunday of August. During this time, a temporary hall is erected at the shrine’s original location, and the mikoshi is moved there, recreating the scene of its ancient enshrinement. * '''Shinji Noh''' (May 15): Alongside the grand festival, ritual Noh performances are held annually on {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}}. ==References== {{reflist}} == External Links == * [http://oonominato.web.fc2.com/ Official Website of Ōnominato Shrine] (in Japanese) {{Normdaten}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{translated page|ja|大野湊神社|version=101992149|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{Draft categories| [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] }} [[every:Onominato Shrine]] [[every:Onominato Shrine|Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[sn:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:draft:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:Onominato Shrine]] [[fr:Onominato-jinja]] [[fr:User:Onominato Shrine]] [[ja:%E5%A4%A7%E9%87%8E%E6%B9%8A%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[sn:Onominato Shrine]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]]

{{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}}: {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}} | map = {{location map|Japan Ishikawa|label=大野湊神社|coordinates={{coord2|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E|}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E}}}} }} '''Onominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a [[Beppyo shrine]] in [[Kanazawa]], [[Ishikawa Prefecture]].{{Cite web |title=Onominato Shrine - 金沢市観光デジタルマップ {{!}} プラチナマップ |url=https://platinumaps.jp/d/kanazawa-city?s=15337&culture=en |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=プラチナマップ {{!}} platinumaps.jp - Platinumaps |language=en}} enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. It is related to {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|en|Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=draft}} == History == According to [[Japanese mythology]] {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en}}, the main god of the shrine, was discovered in the sea during a voyage by an individual named Sana from [[Mutsu Province]] in the year 727. Upon enshrining the deity in the gold stone Masagoyama pole forest, it was bestowed the name "Sanatake Daimeijin."enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. The shrine was originally on a beach, but the shrine was moved to its present site in 1252 following a fire that destroyed the original structure. The shrine faced destruction again during the turmoil of the [[Ikkō-ikki|Ikko-ikki rebellions]]. It was restored by [[Maeda Toshiie]] in 1586. Later, in 1639, [[Maeda Toshiie]], the third feudal lord, constructed three primary shrines within its precincts. In 1872, it became a village shrine and subsequently gained reverence in 22 neighboring towns, including Kanaiwa Town. By 1879, it received the status of a prefectural shrine. Presently, it stands as an individual shrine affiliated with the Association of Shinto Shrines. [[File:Ujikofuda dark reverse.jpg|thumb|An [[Ujikofuda]] from {{ill|Onominato Shrine|ja|大野湊神社|qq=draft}}]] == Subshrines == [[Hachiman shrines|Hachiman Shrine]]: Enshrines [[Hachiman]] also known as [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]]. [[Shinmei shrines|Shinmei Shrine]]: Situated to the right, this shrine is dedicated to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Okami]]. Sanabu Shrine: Positioned to the left, it venerates the Okami of Sanatake, {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en}}. == Cultural property == In 1982, the three main shrines of Onominato Shrine were declared cultural assets of Ishikawa Prefecture. The [[Chinju no Mori]] of the shrine, and its older worship hall, along with various documents, are recognized as cultural properties. The Shinto ritual Noh, emblematic of Kanazawa's traditional culture, has been staged more than 400 times since 1604. The shrine's summer festival stands out in Kanazawa for its magnitude and splendor, and has been labeled an intangible folk cultural asset of Kanazawa City. [[Maeda Toshiie]] promoted Noh, and his son revived its practice at this shrine.https://www.city.kanazawa.ishikawa.jp/f-living/english/KanazawaTradCulture_EN.pdf ==Japanese content== [[File:Noh stage Ohnominato jinja2.jpg|thumb|200px|A Noh stage where {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} is performed]] '''Ōnominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Kanazawa City|ja|金沢市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|qq=draft}}, enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} as its deity. == History == In {{ill|Shinki era|ja|神亀|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|Year 727|ja|727th year|qq=draft}}), a man from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|qq=draft}} named Sana (さな) discovered {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft}} during a voyage. He established a small shrine next to an existing {{ill|Shinmei Shrine|ja|神明社|qq=draft}} (dedicated to {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft}}) at Ōno-shō Masagoyama Saonohayashi. From this enshrinement, the shrine became known as Ōnominato Shrine, serving as the guardian deity of the harbor of Ōno-gō (the old {{ill|Miyakoshi|ja|宮腰|qq=draft}} area, now {{ill|Kanaiwa-chō|ja|金石町|lt_ja=金石町|lt=Kanaiwa-chō|qq=draft}}). In {{ill|Tenpyō|ja|天平|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|729|ja|729th year|qq=draft}}), it was granted the title "Sanatake Daimyōjin" (佐那武大明神). During {{ill|Enchō (Japan)|ja|延長|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft}}), the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft}} listed it as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Kaga District (Kaga Province)|ja|加賀郡 (加賀国)|lt_ja=加賀郡|lt=Kaga District|qq=draft}}, one of the 2133 recognized {{ill|Imperial shrines of national significance (Kunpeisha)|ja|国幣小社|qq=draft}}. Historically, it was also known as Sanatake Ōmiya Daimyōjin or {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft}} Myōjin. By the late {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft}}, the name "Ōnominato Shrine" had faded, replaced by "Sanatake-sha." Around that time, the shrine became a prominent subordinate shrine of the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (noted in the text {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft}}). Today, the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine on the precincts is a remnant of this history. In {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft}} 4 ({{ill|1252|ja|1252nd year|qq=draft}}), a fire forced the shrine to be relocated from Furū-Ōno to the Rikyū Hachiman Shrine area in Teranaka-machi (its current location), approximately eight chō (roughly 872 meters) east. During the {{ill|Sengoku Period|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|qq=draft}} it fell into ruin but was later restored by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家|qq=draft}}. From {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|qq=draft}} 9 ({{ill|1604|ja|1604th year|qq=draft}}), the performance of {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft}} became an annual tradition initiated by {{ill|Maeda Toshinaga|ja|前田利長|qq=draft}}. The shrine buildings were constructed by {{ill|Maeda Toshitsune|ja|前田利常|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|qq=draft}} 16 ({{ill|1639|ja|1639th year|qq=draft}}). In {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft}} 18 ({{ill|1885|ja|1885th year|qq=draft}}), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft}}, and in {{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft}} 41 ({{ill|1966|ja|1966th year|qq=draft}}), it was recognized as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft}}. In Shōwa 57 ({{ill|1982|ja|1982nd year|qq=draft}}), it was designated as a cultural property by Ishikawa Prefecture. Every year, the grand festival held from August 1 to 3 reenacts the shrine’s earlier era when it stood in Ōno-gō for 525 years. A portable shrine (mikoshi) is moved to a temporary hall on the seashore, an event widely known as the summer festival of {{ill|Kanaiwa (Kanazawa City)|ja|金石 (金沢市)|lt_ja=金石|lt=Kanaiwa|qq=draft}}. == Origin of the name and Related Aspects == It is said that the name "Sana" (佐那), the man who first enshrined Sarutahiko Ōkami, is the origin of the shrine’s historical appellations. According to a folkloric interpretation, Sana may refer to "sanagi" (a type of bell, as mentioned in the {{ill|Ruijū Myōgishō|ja|類聚名義抄|qq=draft}}), implying a connection to ironworking technology passed on from northern Japan by gold merchants from Ōshū. Additionally, some theories connect Sana to the deity {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}} worshipped at this shrine, linking it to Hakusan faith. Another theory states that Sana is derived from {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft}}, a sand dune once located along the southern bank of the {{ill|Saigawa River (Ishikawa)|ja|犀川 (石川県)|lt_ja=犀川|lt=Saigawa River|qq=draft}}, near what is now Kanaiwa-chō in Kanazawa City. Originally located at the foot of Saradake by the port of Ōno, Ōnominato Shrine is said to have been lost to the sea due to repeated storms and tidal erosion. By the early modern period, even the name "Saradake" had vanished. According to the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft}}, Taira no Moritoshi (越中前司{{ill|Taira no Moritoshi|ja|平盛俊|qq=draft}}) once encamped at Saradake in Miyakoshi (Miyano-koshi). Additionally, since Sara, Sana, and Sara(dake) appear phonetically and contextually related, it hints at a potential connection between Hakusan Hime Shrine and Ōnominato Shrine. One interpretation is that Sanatake-sha, enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine, was once a subordinate shrine of the Hakusan main sanctuary. The princess deity and Karasaki Myōjin’s child, Prince Sara, may have been worshipped at Saradake as {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft}}, linking these shrines and locations together. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation, the place name "Miyakoshi" can be understood as "the shrine (miya) at the foot (koshi) of a mountain," referring either to the base of Hakusan or Saradake. In ancient Japanese, "koshi" means the foot of a mountain, reinforcing this theory. == festivals == * '''Grand festival:''' Traditionally held from {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft}} to {{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft}}, it now ends on the first Sunday of August. During this time, a temporary hall is erected at the shrine’s original location, and the mikoshi is moved there, recreating the scene of its ancient enshrinement. * '''Shinji Noh''' (May 15): Alongside the grand festival, ritual Noh performances are held annually on {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft}}. ==References== {{reflist}} == External Links == * [http://oonominato.web.fc2.com/ Official Website of Ōnominato Shrine] (in Japanese) {{Normdaten}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{translated page|ja|大野湊神社|version=101992149|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{Draft categories| [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] }} [[every:Onominato Shrine]] [[every:Onominato Shrine|Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[sn:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:draft:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:Onominato Shrine]] [[fr:Onominato-jinja]] [[fr:User:Onominato Shrine]] [[ja:%E5%A4%A7%E9%87%8E%E6%B9%8A%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[sn:Onominato Shrine]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]]

[[User:Lizthegrey|lizthegrey]] ([[User talk:Lizthegrey|talk]]) 08:23, 7 December 2023 (UTC)}} ---- {{infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Onominato.jpg |deity={{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}|Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Ōnominato Shrine | image = [[File:Onominato Shrine.jpg|250px]]
main hall (Haiden) | caption = | map_type = Japan Ishikawa | coordinates = {{Coord|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E|display=inline,title|qq=draft}} | location = Teranaka-machi Ha 163, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikawa Prefecture|qq=}} {{ill|Kanazawa City|ja|金沢市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazawa City|qq=}}, Japan | deity = {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor), Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} | founded = {{ill|Shinki era|ja|神亀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinki era|qq=}} 4 ({{ill|Year 727|ja|727th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Year 727|qq=}}) | festival = Grand festival: {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 1|qq=}}–{{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 3|qq=}}
{{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinji Noh|qq=}}: {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/May 15|qq=}} | map = {{location map|Japan Ishikawa|label=大野湊神社|coordinates={{coord2|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E|}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|35|45.8|N|136|35|54|E}}}} }} '''Onominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a [[Beppyo shrine]] in [[Kanazawa]], [[Ishikawa Prefecture]].{{Cite web |title=Onominato Shrine - 金沢市観光デジタルマップ {{!}} プラチナマップ |url=https://platinumaps.jp/d/kanazawa-city?s=15337&culture=en |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=プラチナマップ {{!}} platinumaps.jp - Platinumaps |language=en}} enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} as its deity. It is related to {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|en|Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=}} == History == According to [[Japanese mythology]] {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, the main god of the shrine, was discovered in the sea during a voyage by an individual named Sana from [[Mutsu Province]] in the year 727. Upon enshrining the deity in the gold stone Masagoyama pole forest, it was bestowed the name "Sanatake Daimeijin."enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} as its deity. The shrine was originally on a beach, but the shrine was moved to its present site in 1252 following a fire that destroyed the original structure. The shrine faced destruction again during the turmoil of the [[Ikkō-ikki|Ikko-ikki rebellions]]. It was restored by [[Maeda Toshiie]] in 1586. Later, in 1639, [[Maeda Toshiie]], the third feudal lord, constructed three primary shrines within its precincts. In 1872, it became a village shrine and subsequently gained reverence in 22 neighboring towns, including Kanaiwa Town. By 1879, it received the status of a prefectural shrine. Presently, it stands as an individual shrine affiliated with the Association of Shinto Shrines. [[File:Ujikofuda dark reverse.jpg|thumb|An [[Ujikofuda]] from {{ill|Onominato Shrine|ja|大野湊神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine|qq=}}]] == Subshrines == [[Hachiman shrines|Hachiman Shrine]]: Enshrines [[Hachiman]] also known as [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]]. [[Shinmei shrines|Shinmei Shrine]]: Situated to the right, this shrine is dedicated to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Okami]]. Sanabu Shrine: Positioned to the left, it venerates the Okami of Sanatake, {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. == Cultural property == In 1982, the three main shrines of Onominato Shrine were declared cultural assets of Ishikawa Prefecture. The [[Chinju no Mori]] of the shrine, and its older worship hall, along with various documents, are recognized as cultural properties. The Shinto ritual Noh, emblematic of Kanazawa's traditional culture, has been staged more than 400 times since 1604. The shrine's summer festival stands out in Kanazawa for its magnitude and splendor, and has been labeled an intangible folk cultural asset of Kanazawa City. [[Maeda Toshiie]] promoted Noh, and his son revived its practice at this shrine.https://www.city.kanazawa.ishikawa.jp/f-living/english/KanazawaTradCulture_EN.pdf ==Japanese content== [[File:Noh stage Ohnominato jinja2.jpg|thumb|200px|A Noh stage where {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinji Noh|qq=}} is performed]] '''Ōnominato Shrine''' (大野湊神社, Ōnominato Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Kanazawa City|ja|金沢市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazawa City|qq=}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikawa Prefecture|qq=}}, enshrining {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} as its deity. == History == In {{ill|Shinki era|ja|神亀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinki era|qq=}} 4 ({{ill|Year 727|ja|727th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Year 727|qq=}}), a man from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsu Province|qq=}} named Sana (さな) discovered {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|lt_ja=猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} during a voyage. He established a small shrine next to an existing {{ill|Shinmei Shrine|ja|神明社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei Shrine|qq=}} (dedicated to {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) at Ōno-shō Masagoyama Saonohayashi. From this enshrinement, the shrine became known as Ōnominato Shrine, serving as the guardian deity of the harbor of Ōno-gō (the old {{ill|Miyakoshi|ja|宮腰|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakoshi|qq=}} area, now {{ill|Kanaiwa-chō|ja|金石町|lt_ja=金石町|lt=Kanaiwa-chō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanaiwa-chō|qq=}}). In {{ill|Tenpyō|ja|天平|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpyō|qq=}} 1 ({{ill|729|ja|729th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/729|qq=}}), it was granted the title "Sanatake Daimyōjin" (佐那武大明神). During {{ill|Enchō (Japan)|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō (Japan)|qq=}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927|qq=}}), the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} listed it as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} in the {{ill|Kaga District (Kaga Province)|ja|加賀郡 (加賀国)|lt_ja=加賀郡|lt=Kaga District|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaga District (Kaga Province)|qq=}}, one of the 2133 recognized {{ill|Imperial shrines of national significance (Kunpeisha)|ja|国幣小社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial shrines of national significance (Kunpeisha)|qq=}}. Historically, it was also known as Sanatake Ōmiya Daimyōjin or {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saradake|qq=}} Myōjin. By the late {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}}, the name "Ōnominato Shrine" had faded, replaced by "Sanatake-sha." Around that time, the shrine became a prominent subordinate shrine of the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (noted in the text {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusan no Ki|qq=}}). Today, the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine on the precincts is a remnant of this history. In {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchō|qq=}} 4 ({{ill|1252|ja|1252nd year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1252|qq=}}), a fire forced the shrine to be relocated from Furū-Ōno to the Rikyū Hachiman Shrine area in Teranaka-machi (its current location), approximately eight chō (roughly 872 meters) east. During the {{ill|Sengoku Period|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku Period|qq=}} it fell into ruin but was later restored by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maeda Toshiie|qq=}}. From {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keichō|qq=}} 9 ({{ill|1604|ja|1604th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1604|qq=}}), the performance of {{ill|Shinji Noh|ja|festival能|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinji Noh|qq=}} became an annual tradition initiated by {{ill|Maeda Toshinaga|ja|前田利長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maeda Toshinaga|qq=}}. The shrine buildings were constructed by {{ill|Maeda Toshitsune|ja|前田利常|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maeda Toshitsune|qq=}} in {{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'ei|qq=}} 16 ({{ill|1639|ja|1639th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1639|qq=}}). In {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|qq=}} 18 ({{ill|1885|ja|1885th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1885|qq=}}), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}, and in {{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa|qq=}} 41 ({{ill|1966|ja|1966th year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1966|qq=}}), it was recognized as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}}. In Shōwa 57 ({{ill|1982|ja|1982nd year|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1982|qq=}}), it was designated as a cultural property by Ishikawa Prefecture. Every year, the grand festival held from August 1 to 3 reenacts the shrine’s earlier era when it stood in Ōno-gō for 525 years. A portable shrine (mikoshi) is moved to a temporary hall on the seashore, an event widely known as the summer festival of {{ill|Kanaiwa (Kanazawa City)|ja|金石 (金沢市)|lt_ja=金石|lt=Kanaiwa|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanaiwa (Kanazawa City)|qq=}}. == Origin of the name and Related Aspects == It is said that the name "Sana" (佐那), the man who first enshrined Sarutahiko Ōkami, is the origin of the shrine’s historical appellations. According to a folkloric interpretation, Sana may refer to "sanagi" (a type of bell, as mentioned in the {{ill|Ruijū Myōgishō|ja|類聚名義抄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ruijū Myōgishō|qq=}}), implying a connection to ironworking technology passed on from northern Japan by gold merchants from Ōshū. Additionally, some theories connect Sana to the deity {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko|qq=}} worshipped at this shrine, linking it to Hakusan faith. Another theory states that Sana is derived from {{ill|Saradake|ja|佐良嶽|lt_ja=佐良嶽|lt=Saradake|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saradake|qq=}}, a sand dune once located along the southern bank of the {{ill|Saigawa River (Ishikawa)|ja|犀川 (石川県)|lt_ja=犀川|lt=Saigawa River|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saigawa River (Ishikawa)|qq=}}, near what is now Kanaiwa-chō in Kanazawa City. Originally located at the foot of Saradake by the port of Ōno, Ōnominato Shrine is said to have been lost to the sea due to repeated storms and tidal erosion. By the early modern period, even the name "Saradake" had vanished. According to the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heike Monogatari|qq=}}, Taira no Moritoshi (越中前司{{ill|Taira no Moritoshi|ja|平盛俊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Moritoshi|qq=}}) once encamped at Saradake in Miyakoshi (Miyano-koshi). In the {{ill|Dai Nihonshi|ja|大日本史|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dai Nihonshi|qq=}} (Vol. 230, Biographies 157, concerning Minamoto no Yoshinaka), citing the {{ill|Gempei Seisuiki|ja|源平盛衰記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gempei Seisuiki|qq=}} and Heike Monogatari, there is a passage: ''"Yorimori barely escaped, regrouped scattered troops in Kaga, and held Miyakoshi Saradake. Minamoto no Yukie took his forces toward Mount Shio, suffering unfavorable battle conditions. Hearing this, Yoshinaka led forty thousand cavalry there. Taira no Moritoshi, upon hearing of Yorimori's defeat, fled to Saradake. Yoshinaka then advanced north into Kaga..."'' == Connection with Hakusan Faith == Although the deity enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine does not overlap with that of the {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirayama Hime Shrine|qq=}}, there was a time when it served as a significant subordinate shrine to the Kaga Baba Hakusan Shrine (as noted in {{ill|Hakusan no Ki|ja|白山之記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusan no Ki|qq=}}). This heritage is reflected in the presence of Sanatake Hakusan Shrine as a subordinate shrine within the precincts. The "{{ill|Kaga Shoshinshaengi|ja|加賀諸神社縁起|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaga Shoshinshaengi|qq=}}" states the following regarding Sanatake Hakusan Gongen: ''"Sanatake Hakusan Gongen was one of the nine small shrines of Hakusan Hime Shrine’s sanctum and is said to have been a branch shrine of the main Hakusan sanctuary in ancient times. Back then, many shrine monks (shasō) served at Sanatake Hakusan, and there was a temple called 'Sanatake’s Kannon Hall.' The area was known as Teranaka due to the numerous temples, and the remains are now called Teranaka Village. The place where the Kannon Hall once stood is now called Kannondō Village. In ancient times, there were numerous shrine attendants and monks of Sanatake Hakusan living in this vicinity, but following the turmoil since the {{ill|Chōkyō|ja|長享|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chōkyō|qq=}} era (1487–1488), the shrine personnel dispersed, and the halls and buildings were destroyed by war. The sacred treasures and Buddhist images were barely rescued..."'' Within the network of the {{ill|Hakusan Shichisha (Seven Shrines)|ja|白山七社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusan Shichisha (Seven Shrines)|qq=}}, there are three shrines of the Middle Sanctuary: the main Middle Shrine, the Separate Shrine, and the Saranomiya (also read as Saromiya). Saranomiya (佐羅宮), located in present-day {{ill|Hakusan City|ja|白山市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusan City|qq=}} at {{ill|Sara|ja|佐良|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sara|qq=}}, is identified with the {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|qq=}}. The Heian-period text "Hakusan no Ki" describes Saranomiya as follows: ''"From here belongs Saranomiya. There is another treasured shrine called Sara Daimyōjin, whose honji-butsu (original Buddhist form) is Fudō Myōō. In the fifth year of Tengen (壬午), a sanctuary building was first constructed. The small shrines (Fugen, Monju) are known as Hayamatsu and Namimatsu (Yone-mochi Kongō Dōji). The Taiko no Taki has six sons. The main Buddha is Dainichi Nyorai. In Chōhō 1 (己亥), two buildings were constructed, each five-bay by two-bay, and one lecture hall was begun. Another shrine, called Rokkusho-dō, exists, with two buildings called On’ya. There is also another shrine called Sakaime Myōjin. Azusazawa is Hiraiwa."'' In another document, "Kaga Hakusan Denki no Koto," Saranomiya is described as follows: ''"The sixth is Saranomiya. Its honji-butsu is Shō Kannon (Noble Kannon), and its manifestation is the earth deity Ugayafukiaezu no Mikoto, the fifth divine ancestor."'' A legend recorded in the {{ill|Gikeiki|ja|義経記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gikeiki|qq=}} "Aibatsuyama no Koto," composed sometime between the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nanboku-chō period|qq=}} and the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, provides related lore: ''Benkei said, "…This place is called 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain) because, in Kaga Province, at a place known as Shimo-Shirayama (Lower Hakusan), there resided a female deity in a palace called Ryūgū no Miya. Having spent many years since she first appeared to Karasaki no Myōjin in the capital of Shiga, she became pregnant. Approaching her due month, she decided to return to her homeland to give birth. While traveling through this mountain’s peak (known as the zennjō [zenjō, summit]), she suddenly felt labor pains. The deity supporting her said, 'Your delivery is near,' and cradled her waist, and so the child was immediately born. At that time, the afterbirth blood spilled, hence the name 'Arachi no Yama' (Bloody Mountain). Now you understand the origin of Arashii no Yama, Arachi no Yama." Hearing this, Lord Yoshitsune laughed and said, "Indeed, I knew this as well."'' The child born there is said to be Sara no Ōji (Prince Sara), suggesting a connection with {{ill|Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|ja|佐羅早松神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sara Hayamatsu Shrine|qq=}}. Additionally, since Sara, Sana, and Sara(dake) appear phonetically and contextually related, it hints at a potential connection between Hakusan Hime Shrine and Ōnominato Shrine. One interpretation is that Sanatake-sha, enshrined at Ōnominato Shrine, was once a subordinate shrine of the Hakusan main sanctuary. The princess deity and Karasaki Myōjin’s child, Prince Sara, may have been worshipped at Saradake as {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|猿田彦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko|qq=}}, linking these shrines and locations together. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation, the place name "Miyakoshi" can be understood as "the shrine (miya) at the foot (koshi) of a mountain," referring either to the base of Hakusan or Saradake. In ancient Japanese, "koshi" means the foot of a mountain, reinforcing this theory. == festivals == * '''Grand festival:''' Traditionally held from {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 1|qq=}} to {{ill|August 3|ja|8月3日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 3|qq=}}, it now ends on the first Sunday of August. During this time, a temporary hall is erected at the shrine’s original location, and the mikoshi is moved there, recreating the scene of its ancient enshrinement. * '''Shinji Noh''' (May 15): Alongside the grand festival, ritual Noh performances are held annually on {{ill|May 15|ja|5月15日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/May 15|qq=}}. ==References== {{reflist}} == External Links == * [http://oonominato.web.fc2.com/ Official Website of Ōnominato Shrine] (in Japanese) {{Normdaten}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{translated page|ja|大野湊神社|version=101992149|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{Draft categories| [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] }} [[every:Onominato Shrine]] [[every:Onominato Shrine|Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[simple:User:Immanuelle/Onominato Shrine]] [[sn:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:draft:Onominato Shrine]] [[en:Onominato Shrine]] [[fr:Onominato-jinja]] [[fr:User:Onominato Shrine]] [[ja:%E5%A4%A7%E9%87%8E%E6%B9%8A%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[sn:Onominato Shrine]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]]
